title: Frontend Engineering Roadmap: Zero to Job-Ready
summary: This roadmap guides you from absolute beginner to a hireable frontend engineer. It focuses on building a strong foundation in web standards, modern JavaScript, and React while creating a portfolio that proves your skills.

phases.title: Web Foundations
phases.summary: Master the core building blocks of the web: semantic HTML, CSS layout, and basic JavaScript logic.

milestones.title: Semantic HTML Structure
milestones.outcome: You can write valid, semantic HTML for any page structure.

tasks.title: Read MDN HTML basics
tasks.description: Study the MDN Web Docs guide on HTML elements and document structure. Focus on the difference between block and inline elements.

tasks.title: Build a static resume page
tasks.description: Create a single HTML file for your resume using semantic tags like header, main, section, and footer. Ensure it is valid using the W3C validator.

tasks.title: Practice form creation
tasks.description: Add a contact form to your resume page using input, label, and button elements. Ensure each input has a corresponding label for accessibility.

tasks.title: Review HTML validation errors
tasks.description: Run your resume page through the W3C Nu Validator. Fix all reported errors and warnings to ensure clean code.

milestones.title: CSS Layout Mastery
milestones.outcome: You can create responsive layouts using Flexbox and Grid.

tasks.title: Learn Flexbox basics
tasks.description: Complete the Flexbox Froggy game to understand justify-content, align-items, and flex-direction. Take notes on common use cases.

tasks.title: Build a responsive navbar
tasks.description: Create a navigation bar that stacks vertically on mobile and horizontally on desktop using CSS Flexbox. Use media queries for responsiveness.

tasks.title: Study CSS Grid
tasks.description: Read the MDN guide on CSS Grid. Understand the difference between grid-template-columns and grid-template-areas.

tasks.title: Build a photo gallery
tasks.description: Create a grid-based photo gallery that adjusts the number of columns based on screen width. Use auto-fit and minmax for flexibility.

milestones.title: JavaScript Fundamentals
milestones.outcome: You can write basic scripts to manipulate the DOM and handle events.

tasks.title: Complete JS basics course
tasks.description: Finish the freeCodeCamp JavaScript Basics course. Focus on variables, functions, loops, and conditionals.

tasks.title: Build a to-do list
tasks.description: Create a simple to-do list app that allows users to add and delete items. Use document.querySelector to interact with the DOM.

tasks.title: Practice event handling
tasks.description: Add a 'clear all' button to your to-do list that removes all items when clicked. Use addEventListener for the button.

tasks.title: Debug console errors
tasks.description: Intentionally introduce a bug in your to-do list. Use browser developer tools to find and fix the error in the console.

phases.title: Core Engineering Skills
phases.summary: Deepen your JavaScript knowledge, introduce TypeScript, and learn professional development workflows.

milestones.title: Advanced JavaScript
milestones.outcome: You can use modern JS features like ES6+, async/await, and array methods.

tasks.title: Learn ES6+ features
tasks.description: Read the MDN guide on ES6 features. Focus on arrow functions, destructuring, and template literals.

tasks.title: Build a quote generator
tasks.description: Create an app that fetches random quotes from a public API. Use async/await to handle the promise and display the quote.

tasks.title: Practice array methods
tasks.description: Refactor your quote generator to use map, filter, and reduce for data manipulation. Add a feature to filter quotes by length.

tasks.title: Study closures and scope
tasks.description: Read an article on JavaScript closures and scope. Write three small examples to demonstrate how closures work.

tasks.title: Code review your work
tasks.description: Review your quote generator code for readability. Add comments explaining complex logic and rename variables for clarity.

milestones.title: TypeScript Introduction
milestones.outcome: You can add static typing to JavaScript projects to catch errors early.

tasks.title: Install TypeScript
tasks.description: Set up a new project with TypeScript using npm. Create a tsconfig.json file and compile a simple script.

tasks.title: Type your quote generator
tasks.description: Convert your quote generator JavaScript code to TypeScript. Define interfaces for the quote data and function parameters.

tasks.title: Practice type annotations
tasks.description: Add type annotations to all variables and functions in your project. Use the compiler to catch any type mismatches.

tasks.title: Read TypeScript docs
tasks.description: Study the official TypeScript handbook on types and interfaces. Understand the difference between interface and type alias.

milestones.title: Development Workflow
milestones.outcome: You can use Git for version control and npm for package management.

tasks.title: Learn Git basics
tasks.description: Complete a Git tutorial covering init, add, commit, and push. Create a GitHub account and push your quote generator.

tasks.title: Set up npm scripts
tasks.description: Add npm scripts to your project for development and build processes. Use a bundler like Vite to optimize your workflow.

tasks.title: Practice branching
tasks.description: Create a new branch to add a dark mode feature to your quote generator. Merge it back into main after testing.

tasks.title: Write a README
tasks.description: Create a README.md file for your project. Include setup instructions, features, and a screenshot of the app.

phases.title: Portfolio Projects
phases.summary: Build three substantial projects that demonstrate your ability to create responsive, interactive, and accessible web applications.

milestones.title: Responsive Portfolio Site
milestones.outcome: You have a professional portfolio site that showcases your skills and projects.

tasks.title: Design portfolio layout
tasks.description: Sketch a wireframe for your portfolio site. Include sections for hero, about, projects, and contact. Ensure it is mobile-first.

tasks.title: Build portfolio HTML
tasks.description: Create the HTML structure for your portfolio. Use semantic tags and ensure all images have alt text.

tasks.title: Style with CSS
tasks.description: Apply CSS to your portfolio using Flexbox and Grid. Add hover effects and transitions for interactivity.

tasks.title: Add JavaScript interactivity
tasks.description: Add a mobile menu toggle and smooth scrolling to your portfolio. Use event listeners to handle user interactions.

tasks.title: Deploy portfolio
tasks.description: Deploy your portfolio to GitHub Pages or Netlify. Test the live site on multiple devices and browsers.

milestones.title: API Dashboard
milestones.outcome: You have a dashboard that fetches and displays data from a public API.

tasks.title: Choose a public API
tasks.description: Select a public API such as OpenWeather or CoinGecko. Read the documentation to understand the endpoints and response format.

tasks.title: Build dashboard layout
tasks.description: Create a dashboard layout with a sidebar and main content area. Use CSS Grid for the overall structure.

tasks.title: Fetch and display data
tasks.description: Use fetch to retrieve data from your chosen API. Display the data in cards or a table within the dashboard.

tasks.title: Add search functionality
tasks.description: Implement a search bar that filters the displayed data. Use input events to trigger the search in real-time.

tasks.title: Handle loading states
tasks.description: Add a loading spinner and error message to your dashboard. Ensure the UI remains usable while data is fetching.

milestones.title: Component Library
milestones.outcome: You have a reusable component library with documentation.

tasks.title: Plan component structure
tasks.description: List five components you want to build, such as Button, Card, and Modal. Define the props each component will accept.

tasks.title: Build base components
tasks.description: Create the HTML and CSS for your Button and Card components. Ensure they are flexible and reusable.

tasks.title: Add JavaScript behavior
tasks.description: Add JavaScript to your Modal component to handle opening and closing. Use event delegation for efficiency.

tasks.title: Write documentation
tasks.description: Create a documentation page for your component library. Include usage examples and prop descriptions for each component.

tasks.title: Test components
tasks.description: Test your components in a demo page. Ensure they work correctly with different props and content.

phases.title: Job Readiness
phases.summary: Master React, accessibility, and performance while preparing for interviews and client work.

milestones.title: React Fundamentals
milestones.outcome: You can build interactive UIs with React components and state management.

tasks.title: Learn React basics
tasks.description: Complete the React section of freeCodeCamp. Understand components, props, and state.

tasks.title: Build a React to-do list
tasks.description: Rebuild your to-do list using React. Use useState for managing the list of items.

tasks.title: Practice component composition
tasks.description: Break your to-do list into smaller components such as Item and Input. Pass props between them.

tasks.title: Study React hooks
tasks.description: Read the React docs on useEffect and useContext. Understand when to use each hook.

tasks.title: Refactor with hooks
tasks.description: Refactor your to-do list to use useEffect for side effects. Ensure the component re-renders correctly.

milestones.title: Accessibility and Performance
milestones.outcome: You can build accessible and performant web applications.

tasks.title: Learn accessibility basics
tasks.description: Read the MDN guide on web accessibility. Understand ARIA roles and keyboard navigation.

tasks.title: Audit your portfolio
tasks.description: Use the WAVE tool to audit your portfolio site for accessibility issues. Fix all critical errors.

tasks.title: Add ARIA attributes
tasks.description: Add ARIA labels to your interactive elements. Ensure your modal is accessible with keyboard navigation.

tasks.title: Optimize images
tasks.description: Compress images in your portfolio and use the loading="lazy" attribute. Measure the impact on load time.

milestones.title: Performance Optimization
milestones.outcome: You can identify and fix performance bottlenecks in web applications.

tasks.title: Learn performance metrics
tasks.description: Read the Google Web Performance guide. Understand Core Web Vitals such as LCP and FID.

tasks.title: Profile your dashboard
tasks.description: Use Lighthouse to profile your API dashboard. Identify the top three performance issues.

tasks.title: Optimize JavaScript
tasks.description: Code-split your React app using React.lazy. Ensure only necessary code loads initially.

tasks.title: Minify assets
tasks.description: Configure your build tool to minify JavaScript and CSS. Verify the reduction in file size.

tasks.title: Review performance report
tasks.description: Re-run Lighthouse after optimizations. Document the improvements in your project README.

milestones.title: Interview Preparation
milestones.outcome: You are ready to apply for jobs and handle technical interviews.

tasks.title: Review core concepts
tasks.description: Create a cheat sheet of key JavaScript, CSS, and React concepts. Practice explaining them out loud.

tasks.title: Solve coding challenges
tasks.description: Complete five medium-difficulty problems on LeetCode or HackerRank. Focus on arrays and strings.

tasks.title: Mock interview
tasks.description: Record yourself answering common frontend interview questions. Review the recording for clarity and confidence.

tasks.title: Update resume and LinkedIn
tasks.description: Tailor your resume to highlight your projects and skills. Update your LinkedIn profile with your latest work.

tasks.title: Apply to jobs
tasks.description: Apply to five frontend positions. Customize your cover letter for each application.
